verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis 2 mission launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch date April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC (6:35:12 p.m. EDT)[5] RocketSpace Launch System Launch siteKennedy, LC-39B[6]'; R2: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.'; R4: 'NASA’s Artemis II SLS... lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida on April 1, 2026'; R6: 'Artemis II lifts off... from Launch Complex 39B at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date, time (to the minute), location, and launch site match directly across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission lifted off atop the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The mission launched aboard an SLS rocket'; R2: 'NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket making its first crewed launch'; R4: 'NASA’s Artemis II SLS (Space Launch System) rocket... lifted off'; R6: 'Nasa’s crewed rocket lifts off'
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state SLS as the launch vehicle for Artemis 2.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission is a roughly 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II (April 1–11, 2026) was a crewed lunar flyby mission... Mission duration9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes'; R2: 'From launch the evening of April 1 to splashdown on April 10, the mission is slated to last about nine and a half days'; R3: 'They are expected to spend about eight more days in space'; R4: 'the approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R6: '10-day lunar journey'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it as approximately 10 days, 9-10 days, matching 'roughly 10-day' precisely.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission marks the first crewed trip to the moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'It was the first crewed flight of the NASA-led Artemis program and the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R2: 'Their spectacular launch Wednesday evening marked the first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 (1972).

verifications.claim: The launch time was 6:35:12 p.m. EDT on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and date match precisely in R1.

verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission goal is a 10-day mission around the Moon to test the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II’s mission was a crewed flight test with four astronauts evaluating the performance of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket along with the Orion spacecraft... approximately ten-day trip'; R3: 'Orion spacecraft — nicknamed “Integrity” by the crew — is on a slingshot “free return ” trajectory... 10-day mission'; R4: 'the approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm ~10-day lunar flyby to test Orion/SLS systems.

verifications.claim: The crew consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Crew... commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, and mission specialist Christina Koch... mission specialist Jeremy Hansen from the Canadian Astronaut Corps'; R2: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; identical in others
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew composition listed across all sources.

verifications.claim: The mission name is Artemis II
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: All references title and refer to it as 'Artemis II' (Roman numeral II).
verifications.reasoning: Consistent naming as Artemis II throughout sources.
